name: Cargo cover on high value chips
blurb: Marine and air policies covering GPU cluster shipments where a single pallet carries millions in accelerators.
summary: Marine and air policies covering GPU cluster shipments where a single pallet carries millions in accelerators.

part_3_high_value_red_flags: An exclusion for theft from unattended vehicles would defeat cover for ground transport legs where drivers stop overnight or leave the vehicle briefly.
A sublimit for electronic equipment or data processing hardware that caps recovery far below the actual replacement cost of a pallet of GPU accelerators.
An exclusion for temperature or humidity variation that would deny claims for chips damaged by condensation or thermal shock during air or ocean transit.
A wear and tear exclusion that could be applied to damage from vibration or handling during normal transit.
A pair and set clause that reduces recovery because a damaged GPU is part of a matched cluster and the insurer argues the whole set is diminished.
A packing exclusion that voids cover if the original manufacturer packaging is altered or if the pallet is not secured to the carrier's specification.
manuscript_wording_and_carve_backs: Delete the electronic equipment exclusion and replace with a broad form covering all risks of physical loss or damage to semiconductors including electrostatic discharge.
Add a valuation clause stating that the insured value is the replacement cost of the chips including expedited freight and installation, not the invoice cost.
Remove any pair and set clause so that damage to one GPU in a cluster does not reduce recovery based on the value of the entire set.
Add a theft from unattended vehicle extension with no sublimit for high value ground transport legs.
Add a temperature and humidity change extension covering damage from condensation or thermal shock during air and ocean transit.
Add a delay in transit endorsement covering additional freight and expediting costs if a shipment is delayed due to a covered peril.
Add a cut through clause allowing the insured to claim directly against the reinsurer if the primary carrier becomes insolvent.

part_4_program_structure_and_limits.bi_waiting_period: No standard business interruption waiting period applies to cargo cover because delay in transit is typically excluded unless specifically endorsed.
part_4_program_structure_and_limits.business_interruption: Business interruption is not covered under standard cargo policies, but contingent business interruption for downstream customers can be added by endorsement with a separate sublimit and a defined waiting period.
part_4_program_structure_and_limits.property_eb_equipment: Not applicable as this is transit cover, but electronic equipment coverage is embedded in the marine cargo policy for damage from electrical or mechanical derangement during transit.
part_4_program_structure_and_limits.per_occurrence_primary_excess_layered_pr: Primary marine cargo policy with a per conveyance limit set to the maximum insured value of any single aircraft or ocean shipment, often in the tens of millions for GPU clusters, with excess layers stacked above.

part_2_paper_type_and_limit_structure.cgl_primary: Not applicable as this is a first party marine cargo policy, but the primary layer is typically a marine open cargo policy with per conveyance and per location limits.
part_2_paper_type_and_limit_structure.paper_basis: Occurrence based because marine cargo policies attach to a specific voyage or shipment and respond to loss or damage that occurs during the insured transit regardless of when the claim is reported.
part_2_paper_type_and_limit_structure.excess_umbrella_towers: Excess layers are placed as facultative cargo insurance above the primary marine policy, with limits determined by the maximum value per conveyance and the accumulation exposure at any one transit point.

part_1_core_third_party_liability_exposu: General average contributions if the carrying vessel suffers a casualty and the cargo is required to contribute to the common maritime adventure.
Salvage charges payable to third parties who preserve the high value chips from a peril insured against.
Liability under the both to blame collision clause where the carrying vessel is partly at fault and cargo interests must indemnify the carrier for damages paid to the other vessel.
Liability for damage to other cargo on the same conveyance caused by improper packing or shifting of the heavy pallets of GPU chips.
Liability for customs penalties or fines due to incorrect valuation or misdeclaration of the high value semiconductor shipment.

underwriter_wants_to_know: What is the maximum insured value per pallet and per aircraft or ocean container unit load device?
Are the GPU chips packed in anti static, shock absorbing, and tamper evident packaging with temperature and humidity data loggers?
What is the planned routing including all transshipment points, storage depots, and any high risk airports or ports?
Is there armed or unarmed security escort during ground transport and at any intermediate storage facilities?
What is the total insured value of a single shipment and the maximum accumulation of chips at any one location or on any one conveyance?
Have there been any prior losses, theft attempts, or damage claims on similar high value electronics shipments?
